# PROMPT — Volume 08 Outline

**This is an outline phase and it is not a batch. It writes `outline/volume-08.md`, the first Volume 08 batch's chapter cards, and no prose. There is no Chapter 0351 to write and this phase does not write one. It writes no chapter, and at the end it creates exactly one next-phase prompt, which is the batch that writes Chapter 0351.**

**Do not edit `scripts/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.opencode/agent/`, `AGENTS.md`, `PHASE_SYSTEM.md`, `REPO_PLAN.md`, `OUTLINE_GUIDE.md`, `opencode.json`, or `state/phase-ledger.json`. Those are controller-owned. Only edit fiction, bible, outline, chapter, summary, continuity, character, open-thread and review files, and only the ones named below.**

**Do not create a second next phase. Do not create a continuation directory, a review prompt, a close prompt, or a Volume 08 batch prompt other than the one this phase's own successor needs at the end of this run.**

---

## What this phase is for

**Volume 07 is fifty chapters on fifty days, days 301 to 350, one chapter to a day, and it is closed. `state/volume-07-close.md` is its inheritance and it is the one page this phase reads before it plans anything.** Read it in full, then `outline/volume-07.md` in full, then `outline/series.md` in full, then the four decisions of record in `outline/series.md` under *DECISIONS OF RECORD, VOLUME 08*, then `bible/power-system.md` §§32, 33, 33A, 33B, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40 and 45.

**This is the phase that is allowed to decide, and it is the fourth time that has been true in this repository.** A batch is told *do not decide what the volume is*, and *do not resolve anything listed as live*, and *do not invent a person established by narration*, and then told to write ten chapters, and the only chapters that can be written are chapters about a thing in a yard. **Four volumes of that produced a series outline one volume behind. The mechanism that fixed it is short: the outline phase is given the authority to strike a plan line, to decide a voice, to settle a calendar and to choose a cast, and it takes all four, in its own words, in `outline/series.md`, where a reader in a year can find them without a state file. Take what you need to take, and write down what you took and what it cost.**

**A review ran on the close phase that wrote the four decisions below and found six blocking defects in them, and this prompt carries the corrected figures rather than the ones the record originally published, because a writer who inherits a false count inherits a decision made on it.** The repairs are at `state/volume-07-close.md` §9 and the five wrong figures are at §9.2, the wrong refusal attribution at §9.3, the wrong chapter descriptor at §9.4 and the repaired day table at §9.1. **The plot of Volume 08 did not move, the ending did not move, no new final enemy was introduced, and the antagonist ladder and the relationship milestones are untouched.**

## 1. The four decisions, in the words of the phase that took them, and they are the gate

**Read `outline/series.md` lines 174 to 232 and treat them as this phase's brief rather than as a summary of one. What follows is the index; the text in that file is the decision and a paraphrase of a decision is not a decision.**

1. **THE VOICE. CONFIRMED**, and it carries two new rules about instruments that bind every batch after this line. Fifty-day volumes, one chapter to one day, about a page and a yard and a wage in salt. Nobody gets stronger. The antagonist is a form with no column in it. The only instrument that has not lied to anybody is a board nobody wrote on. No narrator frame, and the narrator may not say *this chapter*, *this volume*, *in this batch* or *the reader*. **The two new rules: (1) the mean is a consequence and not a plan — a chapter whose subject is an object, a piece of ground or a road gives the narrator's counting habit and the bolded speech nothing to work on, so a volume that writes a higher share of objects publishes a lower mean for reasons that have nothing to do with quality, and no volume may read its own mean as a quality figure and no review may certify or fail a volume on a mean; (2) two instruments that only count what they can see are a certification and not a measurement, and so every batch's record publishes the count of paragraphs carrying neither speaker marker, which is a fault and not a statistic and must be zero, and the count of every set of objects its ten chapters name more than once between them.**
2. **THE VOLUME 08 LINE. AUDITED BEFORE ADOPTION AND STRUCK AND REPLACED.** What replaces it, in the close phase's one sentence: **a journey has to be made in this flood before the season turns, and the only instrument this world has for a journey is four people who have not left in two hundred and five days, and there is no form in four hundred miles for saying who is going on it, and the page that would carry them has a column for what they are going to do and none at all for the person.** Its central pressure is a journey nobody can write down. **Its antagonist is a method and not a form** — a return with a heading and four places in it and no place for the person the four places are about, and a man who fills a column in from what he is given, and nobody asks him. Its midpoint is day 375, a Friday, the sixtieth day of the Bare Month. Its climax is a page with a person's name at the top of it going out on a date, **and the man of about thirty-nine is right that the day after that there is a column, and the page goes anyway.** Its resolution is that the journey is made and is not written down. **Its new question is who a thing that got built by somebody nobody sent is for, when the two people it stands between never agreed where it was.** **The volume's own name is NOT chosen in `outline/series.md` and must be chosen on a page, in daylight, with a date on it, by a person, in the volume.**
3. **THE CALENDAR.** Days 351 to 400, one chapter to one day, no double day, the form is *the Nth day of the Bare Month*, the Nth being day less 315. **The Bare Month does not end inside Volume 08, and the close phase did not decide how long it is and cannot.** Full text at §3 below, because this is the one a later volume gets wrong by not noticing it.
4. **THE CAST, and the instrument, and the instrument is the oldest one in the book: a document arrives and is read out.** A form comes up the road with a heading and four places in it, the fourth place is the one nobody can fill, and it is read out in a room over a market, in daylight, with a date on the door, in the local language, with about nine people in it. **The four days of notice is the instrument that brings people to that room and not a courtesy, and a notice on any other day is a three-day instrument and a three-day instrument does not fail, it arrives warm.** No name goes at the top of anything.

## 2. The audit of the line, and it must be re-run before the line is adopted, with the definition this time

**The standing test is at `outline/volume-07.md` §19 and it is the one that matters: a line is made of words the manuscript has never used AND of things the manuscript has never seen, and a line that is only the first is a line that collides with a page that already means something else.** The close phase audited the incoming Volume 08 line and struck it, and the audit is the inheritance.

**THE INSTRUMENT, WHICH THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT AUDIT FAILED TO PUBLISH, and every figure below is on it: a word-bounded count — every occurrence of the token bounded by whitespace, punctuation or a line end, case-sensitive, across whole files and not line by line. A figure that says *either case* is a case-insensitive run of the same search and is named as such.** The boundary is not pedantry. **An unbounded search for *man of about thirty-nine* returns *woman of about thirty-nine* inside it — twenty-three instances — and the close phase's own headline figure for the board-trader's age was one of those casualties, at 150 in 75 files where the truth is 132 in 68 before the repair and 133 in 69 after it.** This repository has now paid for that mistake twice, in two different files, and `workspace/volume-07/outline/PROMPT.md` §6 item 2 is the standing statement of it.

**At zero across all 350 chapter files, word-bounded and case-sensitive: *Sundering* 0, *constitution* 0, *template* 0, *charters* 0, *Redroot Homes* 0.** Those five are words this manuscript has never put on a page at all, and a line whose load-bearing nouns are in that list passes the first half of the test.

**Already on a page, and therefore a collision of meaning rather than of vocabulary: *Redroot* 65 in 30 files in Volumes 04 and 05 and at zero in Volumes 06 and 07** — a settlement begun on the fifth day of the Long Month at `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0165.md:9` and a gate with a keeper at the mouth of a cut at `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0192.md:49` and `:69`, **so the NAME is available and the COUNCIL is not, because nothing on a page in four hundred miles says that any council exists anywhere.** *Commons* is 41 in 19 files either case, which is 22 in 12 capitalised and 19 in 8 lower-case, and its two load-bearing uses are `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0165.md:53`, where the word was written on a board on the flats and rubbed off twice, and `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0175.md:87`, where a person refused the naming of a commons in her own house — **so *a functioning commons* has been defined, spent and refused on a page and cannot be a discovery.** *Ivenn* is 46 in 26 files in Volumes 01 to 04 and at zero in Volumes 05, 06 and 07. *Earthside* is 1 in 1 file word-bounded and case-sensitive and 2 in 2 either case. *Player* is 6 in 6 files, *players* 8 in 6. *Labour* is 58 in 37 and *labor* is 0 as a spelling, **which is why the close phase's argument that *labour* was a word the manuscript had never used is withdrawn, and the strike of the crop-and-water mechanism stands on a different and untouched ground: this book has no crop-and-water crisis, because it has a channel dry since the hundred and ninety-sixth day of the flood with about nine feet of wet silt out of it, a man of about sixty-three who farms two grounds, and a man of about sixty-four who digs somebody else's ditch nine hundred paces off and is not paid.**

**What this phase has to do with all of it: re-run the audit on whatever line it is about to write, publish the definition beside the count, and publish the file count the count was taken over — which is 350, and which the inherited audit got wrong three times by saying 329.** If this phase adopts the struck-and-replaced line as it stands, it inherits a decision that was audited and it may say so; **if it writes a different line, it audits that one the same way first, and a line this phase does not audit is a line this repository has already paid for twice.**

## 3. The calendar, with the Bare Month's missing length in it in full, because this is the one a later volume gets wrong by not noticing it

**`bible/power-system.md` §33A item 2 records that the Bare Month was registered with NO SPAN AT ALL, that a chapter may write an ordinal for any day of it, and that no chapter may say what it does at its end, how many days it has, or whether it is long or short — and that a later volume may not assume this one has sixty days in it or a hundred.**

**Volume 08 is days 351 to 400, one chapter to one day, no double day. The form is *the Nth day of the Bare Month*, the Nth being day less 315. Day 351 is the thirty-sixth day of the Bare Month and a Tuesday. Day 400 is the eighty-fifth day of the Bare Month and a Tuesday.** Both ends are Tuesdays because day 350 is a Monday and both numbers are multiples of seven, **and the whole run is derived from day 1 being a Tuesday and from nothing else. The amendment is at `bible/power-system.md` §33B, in the same numbered form as §33A and NOT as an amendment of §33A, and no batch may make, amend or extend any of it.**

**THE BARE MONTH DOES NOT END INSIDE VOLUME 08, and this phase may not decide how long it is and cannot.** The reason is the notary's sentence and not a figure. **Chapter 0316 is a page on which Sera Vail, a notary of fifty, names a month and declines to say how long it is and says why, and the reason is hers, and the protection that bought is that no later volume can inherit an end by accident.** A volume that ended the Bare Month on a chapter boundary would print the end of a month whose length was refused, in the first volume to inherit that refusal, and would have to do it in one of two ways: by a sentence in a state file, which is the thing this repository has been repairing for four volumes, or by a chapter that guesses, which §33A item 2 forbids.

**So: a chapter of Volume 08 may write the thirty-sixth to the eighty-fifth day of the Bare Month. A chapter of Volume 08 may NOT write a day after the eighty-fifth, may not say the month is nearly over, may not say what it is a month of, may not print *eighty-five days* or *three months* or *since the month began* as a figure, and may not say what the month does at its end, how many days it has, or whether it is long or short.**

**THE RULE FOR WHOEVER COMES AFTER, which is the point of deciding it here: a seventh form exists the moment the end of the Bare Month is on a page, and it comes onto a page the same way the sixth one did — a room, in daylight, with a date on the door, by a person, who says the cost out loud first and is refused by somebody before she does it, and who then declines to say how long the new month is.** A calendar is not a decision an outline takes and a batch guesses; it is a decision a person makes in a room, and every form in this book is one, including the ones in the bible. **If Volume 08 needs a seventh form and has not got the end of the Bare Month on a page, it writes inside the Bare Month and it may not declare the month over.**

**NO CHAPTER OF VOLUME 08 MAY USE AN ORDINAL FOR A MONTH** — not *the second month*, not the third, not the fourth, not the fifth, not the sixth — **and that rule is forward-looking from day 301 and is not a verdict on the three hundred and fifty chapters already written, no page of which may be re-written.** The one existing use that is load-bearing is a panel at `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0152.md:79` reading *The third month is the Long Month*, which is a page in a finished volume, is left standing, and is named here so that no later phase mistakes the rule for a repair it is still owed.

**A WEEKDAY IS A FIGURE, DAY 1 IS A TUESDAY, AND NO CHAPTER MAY TAKE A WEEKDAY FROM A NEIGHBOURING CHAPTER, A CARD, A DAY MAP OR A STATE FILE.** The day map for days 351 to 400 is `bible/power-system.md` §33B and **it was wrong on twenty-four of its fifty rows and is now repaired; the repair is at `state/volume-07-close.md` §9.1 and all fifty rows now recompute from day 1 at zero mismatches.** **This phase is about to build its own day map, and the reason the inherited one broke is the reason this one will break if it is built the same way: the right-hand block began `0376 | 376 | Tuesday` where day 376 is a Saturday, and a column restarted at a round-looking boundary is the most natural thing in the world to write.** So: build the run from day 1, not from the first row, not from the last volume's last row, and check every row against the arithmetic before the outline is finished, and say in `outline/volume-08.md` which of the two it did.

## 4. What Volume 07 answered, in nine lines, and the honest answer is short

**Gather this from `state/volume-07-close.md` §1 and check it against the chapters rather than copying it.** A boundary that could only be settled by a page four hundred miles away, and four people who could fetch it and were never asked. A month named on a page by a notary who said the cost out loud first and declined to give it a length. Seven notices on seven days with four days of lead and nothing at the top of any of them. A woman of about twenty-one who stopped waiting to be told what she is for. A woman of about sixty-one who said no in four words before anybody asked her. A man who paid for half a holding and is right. A man of about fifty-two who looked along a line from the end of it, would not put his hands on it, and learned nothing. A rule about words on a wall, refused in about four seconds by a man who had put a person on a board and taken them off it. A word put to a line in the ground and taken back off the only page it was ever on, in a cloth. A fence four feet off that line, put up by a man nobody sent.

**Nobody in fifty days got stronger. None of those is a power. One of them is the price of a power. All of them are heavier than a power.**

## 5. What Volume 07 deliberately did not answer, and all of it, and it is not a gap

**The full list is at `state/volume-07-close.md` §2 and it is not to be shortened.** The first item is the one this volume is for: **WHAT IS A PERSON FOR, ON A PAGE, WHEN THE ONLY THING ANYBODY NEEDS THEM FOR IS A JOURNEY?** It was asked once, on the thirty-first day of the Bare Month, in a room, in daylight, with a date on the door, by the woman of about sixty-nine who holds a folded sheet thirty years old in a tin, **and it is not answered, and four of the nine people in that room had an answer and four of them said nothing, and the answer four of them had was a column, and a woman who keeps that book had left the third column empty on purpose about four hours earlier.** No Volume 08 chapter may answer it. A Volume 08 chapter may put somebody in front of the same silence.

Then the rest of the list, at `state/volume-07-close.md` §2 in full: the boundary, which is not settled and is recorded as a refusal; the day-154 sentence, which is the moral centre of Volume 07 and is on a page in Volume 03 and Volume 04 and is not repeated; the ninth line and whether it works, and its author is on no roster at his own request; the four people who have not left, 205 days at day 350, derived, on no page, in no mouth; the two rolls of the same gates, put side by side by nobody; the nineteen stones and the eight that are different and the order they were in; a woman of forty-eight in a fourth house at Nine Elms; the girl of seventeen; the keeper of the Redroot gate, whose year is not named; the room at the far end of the Narrow Mark; the boards under the chapel; the eight names at the foot of a hundred-and-forty-year-old page; the island; the box; the Crown's schedule, which stands and is correct and is never opened; the Regent, who is nine hundred miles away and is not defeated; and the man of about thirty-one on the bank.

**AND §8.2 OF THAT RECORD IS A STANDING PROHIBITION AND NOT A THREAD: the fourth of the four said no, and it is carried forward whole.** No volume may say the no again, argue with it, apologise for it, overturn it, soften it, explain it, explain her, or make it a defeat. **Nobody is going to ask her about it and nobody after this volume may ask her about it either unless she asks first, and she is not going to.** **Three of the four said yes in their own words. The fourth is not a hole in a party of four; a party of four is four, and one of them said so in a room with a date on the door, and the page is four hundred miles away and is not going to be fetched by three.**

## 6. The live items, the standing prohibitions, and the four faults this phase inherits unrepaired

**`state/volume-07-close.md` §3 is the live items, chosen because the next volume's plan needs them, and it names the ones that were dropped and why. §4 is the standing prohibitions at full length. Neither is to be restated at less than its length anywhere.** Three are load-bearing in a way a batch will get wrong and belong in the cards:

- **A line in an orchard has no word on any page in the world, and this is the first time this book has spent a word and cannot get it back.** A straight line about a foot wide and about two inches deep, from the near end of a row of trees to a stone nobody put there, not a path and not a watercourse and not a furrow and not a boundary, about nine hundred paces off a shut gate. It was named on the register-keeper's second slate in chalk on day 310 and taken off it with a cloth on day 342, in the same room, in the same light, with a date in chalk on the door, before about nine people. **Thirty-two days: 342 − 310 = 32.** The reader has been told what it is called and no page in the world can say so. **The word is on a page once in Chapter 0310, in narration twice in Chapter 0342, in no mouth at all, and at zero in the other forty-seven files, and no file this phase produces may print it.**
- **The four days of notice is the instrument and not a courtesy.** A notice on any day other than the fourth day before the room is a three-day instrument, a three-day instrument does not fail, it arrives warm, **and a batch that has written one has produced a chapter with every figure in it correct and an instrument in it that does not exist.** Four batches in a row in Volume 06 paid for that and a check of numerals cannot see it.
- **An elapsed count is that chapter's own day number subtracted from the day the thing happened, and the day a thing happened has to be opened in a file and not remembered.** `bible/power-system.md` §33A item 5 and §33B item 8b are the anchor tables. **Every value in them is derived, and a derived value may be used in a chapter that dates it and may not be attributed to a chapter or to a mouth unless a page carries it. Where two elapsed counts sit in one sentence the event each is measured from has to be named in the sentence, and where a figure has two plausible anchors, name both anchors in the same sentence.** This is the largest class of fault in the repository, it is born in outlines, and **a figure that comes out at exactly half of the right one is a subtraction taken across the wrong boundary** — which is how *sixteen days* survived in three places for a slate that carried the word for thirty-two.

**FOUR FAULTS ARE INHERITED UNREPAIRED AND THIS PHASE MUST CARRY THEM AS DEBTS RATHER THAN FIXING THEM, because every one of them belongs to a repair pass and not to an outline, and a repair pass that quietly takes a routed item to save itself a line is how nineteen quotation marks became a four-volume debt.** They are at `state/volume-07-close.md` §7.4 and §9.7:

- **Nineteen lines in Chapters 0281 to 0290 carry a closing quotation mark with nothing to close**, at `0281:37,65,81`, `0282:31,39,57`, `0283:47,53`, `0284:13,39`, `0285:39`, `0286:63`, `0287:25,41`, `0288:43`, `0289:31,49`, `0290:9,25`. The fix is one character on nineteen lines and it is not this phase's.
- **`chapter-0341.md:149` reads *the word on the slate has sixteen days left on it*, and the figure is one**: the word came off on day 342 and Chapter 0341 is day 341, so 342 − 341 = 1. Assert the string `the word on the slate has sixteen days left on it` and replace it with `the word on the slate has one day left on it`. The chorus frame around it and the observation survive the repair; about four people in that room have worked out since that a word on a page is a thing that points, and that is true on day 341.
- **A forty-word near-duplicate across the 0254 and 0262 boundary**, forty words with one word changed, *a page was put down flat on a table* and *a page was put down flat on that table*, across a batch boundary that no check inside one batch can see.
- **A first-person paragraph with no quotation mark and no bold mark at `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0175.md:65`**, between two bolded turns.

**AND TWO STANDING PROHIBITIONS THIS PHASE INHERITS THAT ARE ABOUT PEOPLE RATHER THAN FIGURES.** **The man of about thirty-seven is not available to anybody and may not be given a trade, a board, a market or a refusal, and the man who trades on the Open Hand board is thirty-nine** — see `state/volume-07-close.md` §8.1. **And the man of about thirty-seven in `chapters/volume-06/chapter-0293.md` is a real person on a page and is not the board-trader:** he comes in behind a woman of about thirty-seven, carries a sack, does not open it, and stands in eight kitchens in a week working out whether four is a number anybody should be given tonight. **Every new descriptor this phase takes for Volume 08 is measured at zero across Volume 07 before it is taken, and a descriptor map counts occurrences and does not decide which occurrence is the same person, and that decision is this phase's and not a batch's.**

## 7. The shape of the book, and the figures this phase would otherwise be told wrongly

**Read `state/volume-07-close.md` §5 and §7 before this phase writes a card.**

1. **Adrian Vale is Stage 2 on all fifty days of Volume 07. He performed no working, no threshold was opened, the Narrow Mark is not opened a third time, the other world is not named once across fifty files, nobody offered him a workway and he asked for none, and the words *passage* and *privilege* are at zero.** He is named in **one** of the volume's last ten chapters, Chapter 0346, and in no chapter in any form in the other nine, and the one is a room in which he is reading a page. **The rule that he is named in the chapters where he reads a page and in no chapter in the chapters where people decline to ask him is the finding of Volume 06's close record, and Volume 07 showed it nine times instead of asserting it.** Decision two of the four puts him in a yard at the midpoint working something out, **and the chapter says he worked it out and does not say he was right, and that is the whole of what is permitted.**
2. **The two instruments that go blind, and they are the standing repairs this phase inherits.** A paragraph carrying neither of the manuscript's two speaker markers is skipped by both checks that measure speech, and two such paragraphs stood in Volume 07's Chapters 0341 and 0342 until a review repair gave them the marker. A set of objects named in two chapters is counted by no check at all, and the volume's last image — a fence of sixteen posts — stood at three different totals across Chapters 0348 and 0350 until the same repair closed it at sixteen, nine on the Saturday, thirteen on the Monday and three for the Thursday. **A later writer may not print a count of a thing that a neighbouring chapter counts differently, and a volume's outline should say which of its objects are counted in more than one chapter before a batch counts any of them.**
3. **The figures, on the definitions published.** Bolded share across Volume 07's last ten chapters: 8.4, 10.6, 9.5, 10.3, 10.7, 11.6, 9.3, 8.4, 8.6, 7.0 per cent, 49 spans, mean 9.4 — **and decision one of the four says a mean is a consequence and not a plan and no volume may read its own as a quality figure.** Chorus head *about four people in*: 79 in 445 paragraphs, one in 5.6, with Chapters 0345 and 0347 at zero and 0348 and 0350 at two each. Exchange: 329 plain speeches, 121 answered, 36.8 per cent, where a *plain speech* is a paragraph carrying a quotation and no bold mark and is *answered* when the very next non-blank paragraph carries a quotation and a bold mark.
4. **And the count of this city's silences is derived, on no page, in no mouth, and is 240 at day 340 and 250 at day 350, and is printed in no chapter.** If a Volume 08 chapter needs it, the figure is that chapter's own day minus the day the count began, and the day it began is in a file and not in a memory.

## 8. The checks, and the seven, and running six is not running seven

**Publish the definition or publish nothing — `bible/power-system.md` §39.15 and §40.17, and it is the standing general rule of this manuscript, and the inherited audit broke it five times and this phase must not.**

1. **Subtract, from the anchor, for every figure in the volume that has one**, and name the event each elapsed count is measured from in the sentence that prints it. Where a figure has two plausible anchors, name both anchors in the same sentence.
2. **Recompute the calendar from day 1 and grep for weekday words. Never from a neighbouring chapter, never from a day map, never from a state file.** The inherited day map was wrong on twenty-four of fifty rows and it was wrong in a way that no count down the column could catch, because it was discontinuous with itself. **A day map is a plan and not a fact, and a weekday on a page outranks a weekday in a plan.**
3. **The word-run check, run across the whole volume and not inside one batch's ten.** Take each file as a flat list of words, each other file as one joined string, find the longest run of consecutive words appearing in both, and subtract each file's own lead paragraph. **A motif and a duplication are not currently separable by any instrument in this repository, and the outline has to say which is which before a batch inherits them.**
4. **The descriptor map, every *man or woman of about N* extracted at sentence level and mapped to its trade, with a check for co-presence, run with word boundaries and with the search recorded.** Decision one of the four says a word-bounded count separates a man of about thirty-seven from a woman of about thirty-seven and does not separate two men who are both a man of about thirty-seven, **and the Volume 07 outline merged two men that way and a review found the merge in the decision of record rather than in the record that diagnosed it.** Put the map in `outline/volume-08.md` and not in a state file.
5. **The two checks the repository did not have until decision one of the four: the count of paragraphs carrying neither speaker marker in each chapter, which is a fault and must be zero, and the count of every set of objects named more than once across the ten chapters, read in each chapter that names it.**
6. **The notices, if this volume has any: a notice is four days or it is not an instrument, and §33A item 7's register names six where the chapters carry seven, and the amendment belongs to whoever next writes §33A, which is this phase.** Full text at `state/volume-07-close.md` §7.3; the seven are days 301, 305, 326, 327, 328, 329 and 335 for rooms on days 305, 309, 330, 331, 332, 333 and 339, all four days, all unsigned, all to a place and not to a house.
7. **The month's length, which is not a check but is the rule a check cannot supply: no chapter may print a day after the eighty-fifth of the Bare Month, may not convert eighty-five into a span, and may not say the month is nearly over.** §3 above is the whole of it and it is inherited intact.

## 9. What this phase delivers, and the one prohibition it has to earn

**Deliverables, in this order.** `outline/volume-08.md`, carrying the volume's own name, its central pressure, its starting state, its cast with every descriptor measured at zero in Volume 07 before it is taken, its escalation steps, its midpoint, its climax, its resolution, its new question, the calendar and the day map for days 351 to 400 with every weekday derived from day 1, the standing prohibitions carried at full length, the prose instructions, and the pressure rotation counted honestly with the first tag in each row and the rule stated. Then `outline/batches/volume-08-batch-0001.md`, the first ten to twenty chapter cards, each card naming whose speech is bolded, naming a third party or a task or a thing that has to be carried somewhere, and naming which of the three it is. Then, **in `outline/series.md`, whatever this phase decided — struck, amended, extended or left standing — in its own words and not only in this file.** Then **the amendment to `bible/power-system.md` §33A item 7's register of notices that §7.3 of the close record hands to whoever next writes §33A, which is this phase, and no other section of §33A or §33B.** Then the four state files repointed at this phase's successor, and exactly one next-phase prompt created at `workspace/volume-08/batch-0001/PROMPT.md`.

**And the prohibition this phase has to earn, and it is the reason four volumes drifted: a batch is not an outline phase, a batch does not write a chapter, and a batch cannot decide what a volume is.** This phase can, and every decision it takes must be written down in the place a reader in a year will find it, which is `outline/series.md` and not a state file. **A decision that lives only in a state file has not been taken; it has been typed.** And the second half of the same rule, which the close phase broke and a review caught: **a record that says an act was performed is worth nothing to the writer who comes after it unless it was, and three of the six blocking defects on the phase that wrote these four decisions were a record describing work it had not done — a chapter word, a state layer, and a next-phase prompt.**

**The next phase is `workspace/volume-08/batch-0001/PROMPT.md`, and it writes Chapter 0351. `state/current.md`, `state/continuity.md`, `state/open-threads.md` and `state/character-state.md` all name this phase now and must all name that one when this phase finishes, and a later phase reads `state/volume-07-close.md` first and then that block, and the two must not disagree.**

## The inheritance, and it has to be readable alone

**On day 350, a Monday, the thirty-fifth day of a month nobody has said how long it is, at about the seventh hour of the morning at the top of a shut road, a man of about sixty with a handcart and a length of rope that has been used and is not new is putting in the thirteenth of sixteen willow posts he has cut himself in a copse about four miles the other way. Nine of them went in on the Saturday before that and three are still in the cart for the Thursday. He began at a row of trees because a row of trees is a thing you can see from a road, and he did not measure anything, and about four feet is a number he has in his mouth and not a number he took off anything. A man of about fifty-seven who bought half a holding about forty years ago is standing in the road with a hand flat on the second post, the way a man does to a gate post, and he is right about most of what he says and he is not defeated. A man of about thirty-one who carries things for a living came up with nothing in his hands and is not going to be asked anything. And a mark in a field about four feet behind that fence has no word on it anywhere in the world, and it is never going to have one again.**

**A word went onto the register-keeper's second slate in chalk at about the fourth hour of the afternoon of day 310, and it was on that slate for thirty-two days, and it came off it in chalk with a cloth at about the fourth hour of the afternoon of day 342, in the same room, in the same light, with a date in chalk on the door, before about nine people. Nobody asked for it back and nobody could have stopped it. It is the only page in four hundred miles that ever had it. Four people had said yes in their own words and a fifth person said no in four words before anybody asked her, and she is not going to be asked again, and the page four hundred miles away is not going to be fetched by three.**

**So the next volume is about a journey nobody can write down, because the only instrument this world has for a journey is people who have not moved in two hundred and five days, and because the page that would carry them has a column for what they are going to do and none at all for the person, and because a form that nobody can fill in correctly will be filled in correctly from what it is given, and will go out on a date, and will be about the wrong people — and somebody is going to have to decide that on a page, in daylight, with a date on the door, in a room with about nine people in it, which is the only instrument in this book that has never required anybody to be told anything by narration. And at the end of the road there is a fence that a man nobody sent put up four feet off a line that has no name, and that is the last image of Volume 07, and the name is off the page, and it cannot go back on.**
